summary: 84-foot 1936 timber tower on Blue Mountain (Snohomish Co.); AWS used the site 1942-43; removed or destroyed 1969; footings and a slab reported.

facts.design: 84-foot treated timber tower on the west ridge; sources differ between an L-6 design and an L-7 cab
facts.status_note: Tower came down in 1969; sources differ on whether it was removed or destroyed. Footings and a concrete slab are reported at the site.

staffing.status: Lookout man on site in 1940; AWS use 1942-1943; no later staffing in the sources

access.note: The route starts at a gated road off Sultan Basin Road. The sources do not say whether the public may pass the gate.

visit.trail_note: Willhite lists the route at six miles and 2,000 feet of gain from a start near 800 feet, beginning at a gate 6.3 miles up Sultan Basin Road from Highway 2.

events.note: 84-foot treated timber tower built by S & P and CCC crews, with a ground house for living.
High Rocks station discontinued; the territory it viewed was taken over by Blue Mountain.
Annual report describes a lookout man packing supplies up about a mile of trail with grades of 30 percent.
Washington Forest Fire Association bulldozer built the final mile of road to the site, as a cat road; the association said it let automobiles reach the lookout.
Used by the AWS in 1942 and 1943; a 12x20 garage may have been built. Seattle Filter Center note gives activation March 8, 1942 and deactivation October 16, 1943.
FFLOS says removed; the other three sources say destroyed. The year agrees across all four.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, January 26, 2012.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS register calls the tower an L-6 design; a Washington lookout history page describes an L-7 cab. The story reports both and does not choose.
The FFLOS register says the tower was removed in 1969; firelookout.com, the Washington lookout history page and Willhite say destroyed in 1969. The year agrees, so the story reports both words.

sources.title: Blue Mountain Lookout Site - Snohomish County

notes_for_editor: Four sources agree on the 1936 build, the 1969 end and the 1942-43 AWS use; they differ only on removed versus destroyed and L-6 versus L-7. Access level 'restricted' is my judgment from the gate on Sultan Basin Road; no source says who controls it, and the brief said 'unknown'. Willhite's page has an 'Area of lookout site today' caption that only places the site just northeast of the big slab; its photo credits read 'Jeff Ruckle photo 2024', and a 2007 caption places a hiking group at the footings. No photo URLs were available in the fetched text, so none are recorded. Willhite could not confirm the footings himself on his four walks.
